content.title: NYT Connections Hints Today: Sunday, April 5 Clues And Answers (#1029)
content.text: Today's ConnectionsCredit: NYT / Erik KainIt’s the very first Sunday of April and we have a very challenging NYT Connections to solve to wrap up the weekend. It’s been a lot chillier this month than last, which feels rather out of order to me, but it’s good weather for puzzle-solving. Also, Happy Easter! I hope you cross path with some candy eggs, or at least a good feast.Once you’re done with your daily puzzles, check out my weekend streaming guide. There’s plenty of new TV shows and movies to give you something fun to watch on a chilly spring evening.ForbesWhat To Watch This Weekend: New Shows And Movies To Stream On Netflix, Hulu, Prime Video, Apple TV And MoreOkay, let’s group some words!If you’re looking for Saturday’s Connections guide, it’s right here.How To Play ConnectionsConnections is the second-most popular NYT Games puzzle game outside of the main crossword itself, and an extremely fun, free offering that will get your brain moving every day. Play it right here.The goal is to take a group of 16 words and find links between four pairs of four of them. They could be specific categories of terms, or they could be little world puzzles where words may come before or after them you need to figure out. And they get more complicated from there.There is only one set of right answers for this, and you only get a certain number of tries so you can’t just spam around until you find something. There are difficulty tiers coded by color, which will usually go from yellow, blue/green to purple as difficulty increases, so know that going in and when you start linking them together. You pick the four words you think are linked and either you will get a solve and a lit up row that shows you how you were connected. If you’re close, it will tell you that you’re one away. Again, four mistakes you lose, but if you want to know the answers without failing, either come here, or delete your web cookies and try again. If you want to play more puzzles, you can get an NYT Games subscription to access the full archives of all past puzzles.NYT Connections Hints And Answers – Sunday, April 5Below, we’ll get into some extra hints for each Connections group – Yellow, Blue, Green and Purple – and then the official clues and answers.Here are today’s Connections words:pipepancakepulpitlight switchshellviolinmushroomorbitcoinpasteurizenucleusmagnifying glasselectrongoogoldeerstalkerthe birdAn Extra Hint for Each Connections GroupHere’s an extra hint to help you solve each Connections group today:🟡Yellow group – cell parts🔵Blue group – things you toss or move from one side to the other, figuratively or literally🟢Green group – elementary, my dear Watson🟣Purple group – the first parts of these words become texture-based shortene wordsOne Word for Each Connections Group:Here’s one word from each group to help get you started: 🟡Yellow group – orbit🔵Blue group – pancake🟢Green group – magnifying glass🟣Purple group – mushroomWhat Are Today’s Connections Groups?Alright, the full spoilers follow here as we get into what the groups are today:🟡Yellow group – Atomic structure terms🔵Blue group – Things to flip🟢Green group – Parts of a Sherlock Holmes costume🟣Purple group – Starting with synonyms for “slush”What Are Today’s Connections Answers?The full-on answers are below for each group, finally inserting the four words in each category. Spoilers follow if you do not want to get this far. The Connections answers are:🟡Yellow group – electron, nucleus, orbit, shell🔵Blue group – coin, light switch, pancake, the bird🟢Green group – deerstalker, magnifying glass, pipe, violin🟣Purple group – (goo)gol, (mush)room, (paste)eurize, (pulp)itHere’s the finished grid:Today's ConnectionsScreenshot: Erik KainThis Sunday’s NYT Connections is rated 5/5 by the Connections Bot, and I’m not at all surprised. This one had me stumped from the get-go, though I was fairly certain ELECTRON and NCULEUS went together. Not being that well-versed on atomic structure, it took me a bit to pair them with ORBIT and SHELL, but the Yellow Group was the least of my worries.I am a pretty big fan of Arthur Conan Doyle’s stories, and so I’m not surprised I figured out the Green Group ahead of the Blue Group today. Still, for some reason I didn’t remember that DEERSTALKER is the type of hat the famous detective wore, and I was trying to think if that was movie or something (like The Deer Hunter). But the other words – MAGNIFYING GLASS, VIOLIN, PIPE – eventually coalesced into a pretty obvious portrait of Sherlock Holmes and that jogged my memory.This left the Blue Group pretty exposed, and soon enough I was flipping PANCAKES and COINS with abandon. The LIGHT SWITCH flipped and a light bulb went off over my head, like some Sherlock Holmes revelation. No need to flip THE BIRD, ladies and gentlemen. I was left with Purple words, as is so often the case, but I was able to puzzle out the connection before plugging in the answer. The beginning of each remaining word was a synonym: GOOgol, MUSHroom, PASTEeurize, PULPit. Very clever. A good little mystery, I dare say.How did you do on today’s Connections? Let me know on Twitter, Instagram, or Facebook.Find more guides to Wordle, Strands and the Mini Crossword on my blog where you can also follow me for TV and movie and video game coverage.
